question: Summarize the Qwen3 Technical Report (arXiv 2505.09388): pretraining (36 trillion tokens, three stages), the four-stage post-training pipeline (long chain-of-thought SFT, reasoning RL, thinking-mode fusion SFT, general RL), and how small Qwen3 models (0.6B-8B) were trained via strong-to-weak distillation from larger Qwen3 flagships.
answer:
Qwen3 models are trained via a three-stage pretraining process on 36 trillion tokens across 119 languages [1][2][3]. Stage 1 (30T tokens, 4K sequence length) builds general knowledge [1][2][3]. Stage 2 (5T tokens, 4K length) focuses on STEM, coding, and reasoning [1][2][3]. Stage 3 expands the context length to 32K using high-quality long-context corpora [1][2][4].

Post-training involves four stages to unify thinking and non-thinking modes [2][5][6]:
1. Long-CoT Cold Start: Supervised fine-tuning on complex reasoning problems [2][3].
2. Reasoning RL: GRPO-based optimization for reasoning quality [7][5].
3. Thinking Mode Fusion: SFT combining thinking and non-thinking data, introducing chat template flags (/think, /no think) [7][5].
4. General RL: Preference alignment across diverse tasks [2][6].

Smaller Qwen3 models (0.6B–14B) and the 30B-A3B MoE model use strong-to-weak distillation from flagship teachers (32B or 235B-A22B) [1][7][3]. This two-phase process involves off-policy response distillation and on-policy logit alignment, requiring roughly 1/10 the GPU hours of the full four-stage pipeline [7][5][8].
